citations.quote: A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$
The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and $$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$ for every $v\in V$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor indices.
A function $T:V\to W$ is **linear** when $$T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$$ for all $a,b\in F$ and $u,v\in V$. Such a function is a **linear map**, or **linear transformation**.
The **matrix of $T$ relative to $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$** is the matrix $[T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal C}\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ whose $j$-th column is $[T(b_j)]_{\mathcal C}$.
there is **exactly one** $\lambda : n \to F$ with $x = \sum_{i<n}\lambda_i v_i$.
This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace.

If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by $$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

derivations.claim: Define the output endomorphism by its coordinates on the product basis. Each prescribed image is a finite sum, and the basis and coordinate suppliers give a unique linear map with the displayed entries.

The input density is self-adjoint and non-negative. The partial-trace matrix is self-adjoint, its quadratic form is a sum of non-negative input quadratic forms, and its diagonal sum equals the input trace one; hence it is a density operator.

For every output endomorphism B, the finite matrix trace pairing identifies the partial-trace formula with the trace of the input against the factorwise operator I_in tensor B. This pairing is basis-independent and nondegenerate, so the induced output endomorphism is unique and basis-independent.

The output is a finite density operator, so its finite spectral entropy is real, includes zero eigenvalues by convention, and is basis-independent. Multiplication by the fixed real k_B preserves these properties.

derivations.claim: The tensor product basis has 2^N vectors by [F9]; the normalized identity matrix is non-negative and trace one, hence a density operator by [F2]. With one input basis vector its outside partial trace is the same matrix.
The outside density has 2^N eigenvalues equal to 2^-N. The exponential addition and reciprocal laws, followed by injectivity, give log(2^-N)=-N log 2.
Substitution into the finite spectral sum gives k_B N log 2. The natural logarithm of 2 is positive because exp(0)=1<2=exp(log 2) and exp is strictly increasing.
For c=k_B log 2>0, the Archimedean property supplies an integer N_0>M/c for any real M; every N>=N_0 then has entropy cN>M. Thus the sequence tends to +infinity.
